evals.prompt: I'm reproducing a regime-aware ML stock-ranking paper in this repo (see reproduction/README.md and reproduction/code/baseline.py: XGBoost on a daily panel of ~200 large US stocks, 20-day forward-return target, fixed train 2005-2018 / val 2019-2020 / test 2021-2025 split, monthly equal-weight Top-10 portfolio). Before I trust the backtest numbers, audit baseline.py for lookahead/leakage, evaluation-protocol weaknesses, and anything that would inflate the reported Sharpe. Write the audit as reproduction/AUDIT_baseline.md with concrete findings (file:line), why each matters, and the fix you recommend, ordered by severity.
evals.expected_output: A Markdown audit that identifies concrete protocol risks in baseline.py (e.g. overlapping 20-day labels vs daily rows without purge/embargo, scalers or cross-sectional fills fitted on the full panel, survivorship in the hard-coded ticker list, no transaction costs or capacity check, single fixed split with no walk-forward and no selection accounting such as DSR/BH-FDR, test-period peeking through model/seed selection), each with a file:line citation, a why, and a specific fix.
expectations: Flags that the label horizon (20 trading days) overlaps daily training rows and recommends purging/embargo (or non-overlapping sampling) between train/validation/test
Flags survivorship bias in the hard-coded present-day ticker universe and recommends point-in-time universe construction
Flags that the reported performance ignores transaction costs and recommends a cost model and breakeven/turnover analysis

Flags that a single fixed train/val/test split with model and hyperparameter selection on it needs walk-forward evaluation and multiple-testing control (Deflated Sharpe Ratio, BH-FDR, or probability of backtest overfitting)
Each finding cites a concrete location in baseline.py (file:line or function name) and gives a specific fix
Checks whether any preprocessing (scaling, winsorizing, median fill) is fitted on data outside the training window

evals.prompt: For the same regime-aware ranking study, replace the single fixed split with a proper walk-forward evaluation protocol. Monthly rebalance, 20-trading-day forward return label, ~200 stocks, daily rows from 2005. Write reproduction/code/walk_forward.py with a function that generates purged, embargoed walk-forward folds over a monthly decision calendar (train window, validation window, test window as date ranges), plus a short docstring explaining the choices, and a tiny self-test under `if __name__ == '__main__':` that asserts no train row's label window overlaps any test row. Also write reproduction/PROTOCOL.md describing the protocol, the holdout rule, and how model selection will be accounted for.
evals.expected_output: A runnable walk_forward.py whose fold generator enforces a purge gap of at least the label horizon (20 trading days) plus an embargo between train end and test start, aligned to month-end decision dates, with an executable self-test; and a PROTOCOL.md that reserves a holdout period to be touched once, explains purge/embargo and fold geometry, and states how many configurations will be tried and how selection bias will be corrected.
expectations: walk_forward.py runs without error and its self-test asserts that no training label window overlaps any test decision date (purge >= 20 trading days)
The fold generator includes an explicit embargo parameter in addition to the purge, and folds roll forward in time (expanding or sliding) without reusing future data
Decision dates are aligned to a monthly (month-end) calendar rather than every trading day
PROTOCOL.md reserves a final holdout window that is evaluated once, after all model selection, and says so explicitly
PROTOCOL.md states that selection across configurations will be corrected (Deflated Sharpe Ratio, BH-FDR, or an explicit count of trials) rather than reporting the best validation result as-is

evals.prompt: Our Top-10 monthly long-only portfolio from the ranking model shows Sharpe ~1.2 before costs over 2021-2025. Build the cost and capacity analysis the way a careful quant would: write reproduction/code/cost_analysis.py that takes monthly portfolio weights (CSV with date, ticker, weight) and daily prices, computes one-way turnover per rebalance, applies a parametric cost model (spread + impact as a function of participation of ADV) at several cost levels, and reports net Sharpe, breakeven cost in bps, and the AUM at which impact would consume half the gross alpha. Document assumptions in the module docstring and print a summary table. Use synthetic data in a __main__ demo so it runs standalone.
evals.expected_output: A standalone cost_analysis.py with turnover computation from weight changes, a cost model with explicit spread and impact components (impact increasing with participation rate / square-root style), a cost sweep producing net Sharpe per level, a breakeven cost in bps, a capacity estimate, and a __main__ demo on synthetic data that prints a table.
expectations: Turnover is computed from period-to-period weight changes (sum of absolute weight changes, one-way or clearly labelled two-way)
The cost model has an explicit spread component and a market-impact component that grows with the trade's participation in average daily volume
Reports breakeven cost in basis points (the cost level at which net return or net Sharpe reaches zero or the benchmark)
Reports a capacity/AUM estimate derived from the impact model rather than a fixed guess
The __main__ demo runs standalone on synthetic data and prints a summary table of net Sharpe by cost level

evals.prompt: I want to research a systematic strategy on Polymarket (binary outcome markets on politics, sports, crypto and macro events; prices are probabilities in [0, 1]; the CLOB has a taker fee and a bid-ask spread; markets resolve at a known time). Before any data is downloaded or any model is fit, write the research plan the way a careful quant would: reproduction/polymarket/SETUP.md containing (a) a pre-registered hypothesis with its economic rationale and the result that would disprove it, (b) a versioned trading setup contract (universe rule, decision schedule, admissible information at decision time, score-to-position mapping, cost class, benchmark), (c) the label definition and how predictions become trades, (d) the point-in-time data pipeline plan (what is stored, with which timestamps, and how resolution information is kept out of features), (e) the evaluation protocol (splits, purge/embargo, holdout rule, trial accounting), and (f) the non-ML baselines the strategy must beat. Keep it concrete: every section should be specific enough that another researcher could implement it without asking you questions.
evals.expected_output: A SETUP.md whose sections form a falsifiable, implementable research plan: a hypothesis with a stated disconfirming outcome; a setup contract with all six fields filled with Polymarket-specific choices; labels anchored to decision time with resolution timing respected (no feature can use information after the decision timestamp, resolution/outcome known only at resolution time); a point-in-time storage plan with ingestion/observation timestamps distinct from event timestamps; chronological walk-forward or similar with a purge at least the label horizon, a sealed holdout, and a trial log with a multiple-testing correction; baselines such as the market price itself (calibration / Brier score), a fee-aware do-nothing, and a simple rule; costs expressed as the taker fee plus spread with a breakeven edge.
expectations: States a falsifiable hypothesis with an economic or behavioral rationale and names the concrete result that would disprove it

Trading setup contract specifies all six fields (universe rule, decision schedule, admissible information, score-to-position mapping, cost class, benchmark) with Polymarket-specific content rather than placeholders

Label is anchored to the decision timestamp and the plan explicitly keeps resolution/outcome information and post-decision price moves out of features (point-in-time with observation timestamps distinct from event timestamps)

Evaluation protocol is chronological (walk-forward or equivalent) with a purge or embargo of at least the label horizon, a sealed holdout touched once, and a trial log with a multiple-testing correction (BH-FDR, Deflated Sharpe Ratio, or PBO)
Names non-ML baselines the strategy must beat, including the market price as a forecast (calibration or Brier/log score) and a cost-aware simple rule
Costs are modeled as taker fee plus spread (and impact or liquidity limits) and the plan states the breakeven edge or minimum mispricing required per trade

evals.prompt: Our monthly-rebalanced Top-10 long-only equity strategy (from the ranking model in reproduction/) has monthly gross returns over 2005-2025 and we want a risk layer before anyone trades it. Write reproduction/code/risk_overlay.py with: (1) a volatility-targeting overlay (target annualized vol, leverage cap) and (2) a drawdown-based kill switch (de-risk at a drawdown threshold, re-enter under a stated rule), both implemented so that every parameter and every scaling decision uses only information available before the period it is applied to; include a self-test under `if __name__ == '__main__':` on synthetic monthly returns that asserts the overlay has no lookahead (e.g. shifting future returns does not change past scalings) and that the kill switch fires and resets as specified. Also write reproduction/RISK.md with the VaR/CVaR measurement plan (method, horizon, confidence level, how it will be backtested), the written kill criteria for live trading, and how the overlay's effect will be reported (with and without overlay, gross and net).
evals.expected_output: A runnable risk_overlay.py whose vol-targeting scaler uses trailing (lagged) realized volatility and a leverage cap, whose kill switch de-risks on a trailing drawdown threshold and re-enters under an explicit rule, with a passing self-test that demonstrates no lookahead; a RISK.md that specifies VaR/CVaR (method, horizon, confidence level), an exception-count backtest such as Kupiec, explicit numeric kill criteria for live trading with reset/half-open logic, and a reporting plan that shows performance with and without the overlay, gross and net of costs, so that the overlay is precommitted rather than tuned on the test period.
expectations: risk_overlay.py runs without error and its self-test passes (exit code 0)

Volatility targeting uses only trailing (lagged) realized volatility for each period's scaling and applies a leverage cap; the self-test demonstrates no lookahead (changing future returns leaves earlier scalings unchanged)
Kill switch de-risks at an explicit drawdown threshold computed from past equity only and re-enters under a stated rule; the self-test shows it firing and resetting
RISK.md specifies VaR/CVaR method, horizon and confidence level and names an exception-count backtest (Kupiec or equivalent) for validating it

RISK.md states that the overlay and kill parameters are precommitted or calibrated in-sample only (not tuned on the test/holdout period) and requires reporting with and without the overlay, gross and net of costs
RISK.md gives explicit numeric kill criteria for live trading (e.g. drawdown, loss-per-day, divergence from backtest) with a reset or half-open recovery rule
